title: SME finance is recovering unevenly while high borrowing costs and shorter-term credit constrain investment and resilience
source_unit: OECD Financing SMEs and Entrepreneurs 2026: An OECD Scoreboard
geography: 48 OECD and partner countries, with SME financing indicators covering 2007-2024 and latest available information through 2025

observations.period: 2024-2025; OECD SME Finance Scoreboard covering 48 countries

denominator.unit: OECD and partner countries included in the 2026 Scoreboard

countries_sme_rates_above_pre_pandemic.unit: countries out of 39 with SME interest rates higher than pre-pandemic levels

countries_higher_collateral_requirement_.unit: countries out of 17 showing higher shares of SMEs requiring collateral

countries_vc_volume_increased.unit: countries out of 30 with increased venture-capital volumes

sme_loan_stock.unit: real outstanding SME-loan stock across Scoreboard countries

sme_long_term_loan_volume_change_since_2.unit: percent change in aggregate real long-term SME-loan volumes in the selected country group since 2021

finance_constrained_smes_eu.unit: percent of SMEs reported as finance-constrained in the cited European Commission evidence

observations.method: The OECD Scoreboard combines supply-side data from financial institutions and statistical agencies with demand-side surveys and policy information, covering debt, equity, asset-based finance, and financing conditions.
observations.uncertainty: SME definitions, indicator coverage, inflation adjustment, reference years, and country composition vary. Country counts are not a single pooled firm-level estimate. A higher rate or collateral requirement does not prove credit denial, and a loan-stock trend does not directly measure investment quality or employment.
observations.subgroup: Employer SMEs and entrepreneurs in non-financial sectors, with differences by firm size, age, sector, country, innovation intensity, ownership, and access to collateral or audited financial statements.
observations.counterinterpretation: New lending can recover while the outstanding stock stays flat because firms repay short-term loans; lower applications or long-term borrowing can reflect weak demand, delayed investment, or firms using equity, leasing, factoring, internal funds, or public guarantees instead.

denominator.unit: OECD and partner countries in the Scoreboard; policy instruments and country availability vary

factoring_growth_2024.unit: percent change in aggregate factoring activity in 2024

leasing_growth_2024.unit: percent change in leasing activity in 2024

countries_declining_guaranteed_loan_volu.unit: countries out of 25 reporting declines in guaranteed-loan volumes in 2024

guarantee_median_volume_change.unit: percent change in the Scoreboard median guaranteed-loan volume in 2024

policy_direction.value: diversification toward fintech, asset-based finance, equity, public guarantees, and targeted support

strategic_targeting.value: green-tech, deep-tech, defence, women-owned firms, trade-exposed SMEs, sustainability, digitalisation, and skills

observations.method: The report reviews public guarantees, direct lending, venture-capital schemes, digital factoring infrastructure, invoice registries, fintech-driven finance, and targeted support for strategic or vulnerable SME segments.
observations.uncertainty: A decline in pandemic-era guarantees may represent normalization rather than a loss of support. Public participation in venture capital and fintech expansion do not establish additionality, equitable reach, firm survival, or downstream worker outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Start-ups, innovative SMEs, women-owned firms, trade-exposed firms, green and digital-transition firms, non-bank lenders, public development banks, investors, and firms with limited credit history.
observations.counterinterpretation: Targeted finance can correct market failures and mobilize patient capital, but strategic selection can also concentrate resources in high-visibility sectors or large deals; the report notes that the AI equity rebound is concentrated in a limited number of large investments.

boundary: This record adds a firm-finance and investment-capacity route. It does not identify individual firm trajectories, establish causal effects of credit conditions or public finance, measure worker outcomes, or treat country-level SME indicators as representative of every small business.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: OECD Financing SMEs and Entrepreneurs 2026 publication page, executive summary, recent-trends chapter, and official PDF retrieved; country counts, loan-stock, long-term-credit, interest-rate, collateral, venture-capital, asset-based-finance, guarantee, fintech, and policy-response claims cross-checked against the publication.
